- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 3–5% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.2) or shows sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 3–5% to account for volatility.  
- After a price spike (forecast > history mean + 10%), model frequently overcorrects; cap forecast at +5% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., 0.6→0.1→0.8), model overfits recent trends; apply 3-period smoothing to forecast.  
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after 10–15 day downtrends; add 1–2% buffer to forecast for downward corrections.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture mean reversion; if 20-day average is > 10% above recent 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 5–8%.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple 1.00 values, model tends to overreact; apply sentiment decay factor (e.g., 0.95 per 3-day window) to dampen forecast.
